messages.subject: Summary of Protein intensities
messages.body_plain:
Dear Olga and Meena

By using the command quantification function which uses my dataProcess output as data input, i get a table with summarized abundance/intensity values for each protein within each group or sample. I would like to understand better how this summary is actually done.
As far as I got from my data this summary is not just the sum or the average off all transitions of a particular protein.
How are the individual transitions intensities actually summarized to get a final intensity?

And how is the group intensity assessed? From my data it seems as if it would be the average of the individual sample summaries of a particular group. Is this correct?

According to the personal e-mail you sent me, for the global standard normalization MSStats also bases its normalization procedure on a summarized intensity of the standard protein (aka. "subject quantification"). Does this work similar to the summarizing process done by the function quantification()? If not, what would be different?

many thanks and best regards

Christian

messages.subject: Re: Summary of Protein intensities
messages.body_plain:
Dear Christian,

Sample-level quantification is done based on linear mixed models described in this reference http://www.biomedcentral.com/1471-2105/13/S16/S6/abstract
In some special cases (i.e., when all features have the same variance in all conditions, and have no missing values) the model-based summaries are identical to averages on the log scale.

The same procedure is used for the standard proteins and for all the other proteins.

Sincerely
Olga
